description: Reproducing PROC LIFETEST life-table (actuarial) survival estimates: METHOD=LT over fixed intervals, Greenwood variance, complementary log-log confidence limits, PDF and hazard with their limits, per strata.

actuarial_life_table.title: METHOD=LT builds an actuarial life table with effective sample size n' = n_enter - (censored/2).
rule: The actuarial (life-table) estimator groups event/censor times into fixed-width intervals (set by NINTERVAL= or a width) and computes, per interval i:
- n_enter[i]: number at risk entering the interval (previous entrants minus prior events and prior censored).
- d[i]: events in the interval; w[i]: censored in the interval.
- effective at risk n'[i] = n_enter[i] - w[i]/2  (censored assumed at risk for half the interval).
- conditional event prob q[i] = d[i]/n'[i]; survival prob within interval p[i] = 1 - q[i].
- Survival S at interval boundaries is the cumulative product of p over prior intervals (S[0] = 1).
Process each STRATA group independently; a FREQ variable weights each record's contribution to n_enter, d, and w.
SAS trims trailing intervals after the last one containing any event or censoring.
pitfalls: Kaplan-Meier (METHOD=KM/PL) is a DIFFERENT estimator (jumps at event times, no half-censored adjustment). Do not mix it with METHOD=LT.
Omitting the w/2 half-interval adjustment in n' biases every downstream quantity.
Survival is defined at interval BOUNDARIES (one more than the number of intervals); off-by-one errors shift the whole curve.

greenwood_and_cloglog_ci.title: Variance is Greenwood's formula; default confidence limits use the complementary log-log transform.
rule: Greenwood variance of S at a boundary: Var(S) = S^2 * sum_over_prior_intervals( q[j] / (n'[j] * p[j]) ).
SAS default survival confidence limits use the complementary log-log (log of the cumulative hazard) transform, which keeps limits inside [0,1]:
- Let H = -ln(S), then CI on ln(H) is ln(H) +/- z * se_g, where se_g = se(S) / (S * H) and z = normal quantile for the chosen alpha.
- Back-transform: limits on S are exp( -exp( ln(H) +/- z*se_g ) ) (note the sign swap maps to lower/upper).
- Clamp to [0,1]; when S is 0 or 1 the limits collapse to that boundary.
PDF and HAZARD each have their own variance-based limits over the interval; report them only where the estimate is defined (q>0, n'>0).
pitfalls: Using a naive symmetric (linear) CI S +/- z*se(S) can exit [0,1] and will not match SAS defaults (which are cloglog).
Dividing by zero when p or n' is zero: guard those intervals and carry the previous cumulative variance forward.
